title: Turning the trombone around in South Bend
summary: He took a job in South Bend with Tom Brown and William Barbee, played left-handed for months, then turned the horn around for good and practiced baritone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: I mean, it stayed with me because that was really a major disappointment in my life by not getting in that band. So I thought about what he had said. And shortly afterwards, I get a job to go with the group in South Bend, A Downer. So I had definitely made up my mind, I say. Because these fellas that I was going to work with, I mean, they were all new to me. I didn't know anything about them because it was different category of musicians and different fellas that I didn't know at that time. So I say, well, I'm going on this job and I'm going to try and make good. I'm going to try to play enough to get myself in their set and say, after I think that I'm in their set, I'm going to turn that instrument around one day and never turn it back again. And that's what I did. I went on out on this job and it was a terrific band, very good band. And the band was Tom Brown, who, he's in the Orleans Clanniers, two very, very good and wonderful pianists. William Barbee, you may have heard of him. He's on some of those records. Yeah, he made some records with Cine. Yeah, and he made some with me too.
Oh, I didn't know. Yeah, he's on some of those records with me.
So, I played my usual left hand way for about two or three months until I got set pretty good with the fellas. And one night I turned the horn around and I say, I never will turn it back again.
Well, it was almost like starting all over again. Did you practice at home?

Yeah, I would practice. We were living right up over the place that we were playing. We were playing in a cabaret and it was a hotel and everything. So, I would practice and I could play baritone, which at that time was a novelty up here, I mean getting off on the baritone at home. So, when I'd get tired or something would get too difficult for me to make on the slide with my left hand, I would pick up the baritone. And you'd use left hand on that, did you?
